THE CHANGE: emit the #300 context manifest from checklist_engine.start() and reopen() — the two and only two sites that set status 'in-progress' (:1635, :1852), which advance() at :1644 requires. g2-implement.title: Mechanical composer: the field group from engine state alone
g2-implement.imperative:
Fill the handoff and dispatch constellation-implementer. THE CHANGE: a composer that fills the frozen mechanical field group from engine state with zero agent effort, emitted as a snapshot at the SAME seam as g1 so a run where the agent records nothing still yields the full group. Field sourcing is ADJUDICATED, not the implementer's choice: run=cl['work_id']; project=the MAIN CHECKOUT's name via durable_root(), NOT Path(worktree).name which yields 'e298-305' and would give the same repo a different project every epic; role=the lease's claimed_by; spine-step=active_id(cl), the one selector, imported never re-derived; context-manifest-ref='ctx-<work-id>-<step>@<rev>' where rev is context_manifest.rev() over the manifest's own bytes - this satisfies EPISODE_STORE.md:679-689's <manifest-ref>@<revision> contract verbatim ('pinning to its own blob hash at capture time') and is why g1's write-if-absent is load-bearing; rework-count from task['rework_count']; reopens from the journal's reopen entries; failed-commands from evidence type command-output with payload.exit != 0 - these survive a refusal because the evidence item is appended BEFORE the raise and main() persists on the error path; artifact-ref from _collect_changed_files() (:607), which already returns REPO-RELATIVE paths matching the shipped episodes' shape - do NOT invent an 'artifact-ref' evidence type, it has zero occurrences across ~900 evidence items and would be a second secretly-agent-dependent field.

REFUSALS - THE FLOAT IS ANSWERED: the Admiral ruled it IS IN SCOPE. A refusal today raises EngineError, main() catches it at :2556 and DOES persist cl, but records nothing about the refusal; the journal sidecar is documented and implemented as success-only (:2469, append_journal_entry sits after the return 1). So the field has no engine-state source and is today secretly agent-dependent, which decision:zero-agent-effort-is-literal forbids. Add the counter on main()'s except EngineError path, which already calls save(). FOUR CONDITIONS, all non-negotiable: (1) ADDITIVE ONLY - no existing field changes meaning, no existing reader breaks on a checklist that lacks the counter. (2) docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md is updated IN THIS SAME PR - a schema change shipped with a stale doc is the exact defect #309's sweep found live, so this is not a follow-up. (3) PROVE THE COUNTER CAN BE WRONG, and prove that test can fail: induce a real refusal, assert the counter incremented to the specific expected value, then break the increment and confirm the test goes RED on that specific assertion - not merely non-zero exit, which an import error also produces. (4) STATE THE LATENCY in the result: the engine change is latent until the installed corpus is refreshed (#344), so refusals will be silently absent in production while these tests pass. That is a real gap to report, not to engineer around.

ALSO CORRECT docs/EPISODE_STORE.md:781. It currently says '#305 wires automated capture - nothing writes to this store on its own yet', which promises something the store's own validator forbids: _validate_create requires all five agent-supplied assertion kinds with non-empty statements, so a complete episode CANNOT exist without agent judgment. The adjudicated reading, ruled by the Admiral: #305 delivers a MECHANICAL SNAPSHOT, not auto-created episodes. The acceptance criterion says 'the full mechanical FIELD GROUP', not a complete episode. Rewrite that line so a reader of main sees the true division: the mechanical half falls out of the engine with zero agent effort; the judgment half stays agent-initiated because it is irreducibly judgment.

REFUSE, NEVER FABRICATE: if any field cannot be honestly sourced, the assembler REFUSES rather than emitting a silent 0 or a plausible default. A fabricated mechanical fact is worse than an absent one. Wait for and integrate IMPLEMENTER_RESULT.

constraints: PROJECT SOURCING IS CORRECTED -- do NOT use durable_root() for it. The plan previously said project = Path(durable_root()).name, on D5's reasoning that durable_root() yields the MAIN CHECKOUT and so keeps 'project' stable across epics. That reasoning is wrong, and I proved it empirically rather than by reading: durable_root() returns the worktree unchanged whenever an ACTIVE ADMIRAL EPIC LEASE exists (agent_work_root.py, the _active_epic_lease branch: 'the main checkout is fenced read-only, so honor the worktree'). That is exactly the condition every commander in this epic runs under. Measured in this worktree: durable_root(cwd) -> C:/Programs/constellation-skills-wt/e298-305, so Path(...).name -> 'e298-305'. That is precisely the per-epic drift D5 existed to prevent, reintroduced by the fix D5 prescribed. Corroborated by a real emitted manifest at .agent-work/issue-305/context/g1-review.json, whose run.roots.durable reads the worktree path.

USE INSTEAD: the parent of `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, resolved absolute, and take its basename. Measured here: -> C:/Programs/constellation-skills -> 'constellation-skills'. This is correct on ALL THREE paths, which is why it beats durable_root() for this one field: in a linked worktree --git-common-dir points at the main checkout's .git regardless of any lease; in a plain checkout it returns '.git', whose parent is the checkout root; and it is unaffected by epic leases entirely, because it asks git about repository topology rather than asking the work-area helper about writability. Those are different questions and the field wants the first one.

FALLBACK, and it must REFUSE rather than guess: if git is absent or the directory is not a repository, the composer REFUSES to emit `project` rather than falling back to the worktree basename. A worktree-derived project silently poisons the one join meant to survive worktree deletion, and a fabricated mechanical fact is worse than an absent one. This is the same refuse-never-fabricate rule the gate already carries for `role` and `refusals`.

PROVE IT THE WAY IT WAS MISSED: a test asserting `project` is stable must be run FROM A LINKED WORKTREE UNDER AN ACTIVE EPIC LEASE, because that is the condition under which the old formula was wrong and every other condition it was right. A test that only exercises a plain checkout passes on the broken formula -- that is how D5 shipped its own defect. Cover both sides.

g3-implement.title: Negative control, proof it can fail, and cross-run retrieval
g3-implement.imperative: Fill the handoff and dispatch constellation-implementer. THE CONTROL: drive a real spine where the agent records NOTHING beyond what postconditions mechanically require, then assert the full mechanical field group is present AND CORRECT. Correctness is asserted against an INDEPENDENTLY-TALLIED GROUND TRUTH — the harness records each induced event at the moment it issues the triggering call, then compares field by field. DO NOT use apply_episode_delta.validate_delta() as the oracle: it is type-and-presence only (isinstance(str) and value.strip() for every string field), so a composer returning nine hardcoded constants passes it, and so does the delete-one-field red-proof, because deleting a key from a dict is independent of how the dict was filled. That control proves the validator rejects incomplete input, never that capture works. The validator stays in the pipeline as a shape check on the way to the writer; it is not the oracle. PROOF THE CONTROL CAN FAIL: run it against a deliberately incomplete capture — revert the composer to constants, or drop one derivation — and confirm it goes RED, asserting the SPECIFIC failed field, not merely non-zero exit. A wrapper that maps any non-zero to red also reports red for an import error or a collection failure; assert the specific assertion. Then CROSS-RUN RETRIEVAL: seed episodes, mark one cluster consolidated, confirm rhyme-search still finds its neighbours, and DISCARD the synthetic consolidation — a test artifact must never become canon; confirm the discard by normalized content or blob OID, never raw working-tree bytes (#319). Wait for and integrate IMPLEMENTER_RESULT.
